title: Smoothing reservations and adaptive autoscale roadmap for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a quarterly roadmap that reduces cost volatility for Dedicated customers by introducing reservation smoothing and an adaptive autoscale policy that respects SLOs. This ticket captures scope for experiments, MVP controls in the Console, metric tracking, and rollout gating criteria. The objective is to make committed capacity less brittle to sudden traffic swings while preserving latency SLAs and predictable billing for customers.
background: Enterprise customers buying Reserved Pools report two recurring issues: (1) sudden usage spikes force expensive burst charges or throttling, and (2) committed unit refunds/adjustments are painful when teams overcommit. Current autoscale rules are reactive and metric thresholds are brittle across workloads. We need a principled approach combining reservation smoothing (time-windowed hedging) and adaptive autoscale that adjusts aggression based on recent latency and queueing signals.
objectives: Define an MVP smoothing algorithm for reservation hedging that shifts small portions of commit between adjacent billing windows
Implement an adaptive autoscale policy that factors latency SLO violations and KV cache hit rates to decide scale-up urgency
Expose controls in Redwood Console for admins: smoothing window, hedge percentage, failback sensitivity
Run canary with 3 pilot customers and measure unit cost delta and SLO adherence over 6 weeks
success_metrics: Reduce monthly burst spend for pilot customers by >=15% without increasing P99 latency by >5%
Decrease customer-initiated reservation adjustments by 30% across pilots
New autoscale policy respects latency SLOs (P95 under SLA target) in 95% of autoscale events
Console adoption: admin toggles smoothing feature on >=50% of pilot pools
roadmap_milestones: Week 1-2: Spec finalized and engineering spike to prototype hedge algorithm (simulation harness)
Week 3-5: Implement autoscale policy primitives in Dedicated control plane (feature flagged)
Week 6-7: Console UI for smoothing controls and rollout gating pages
Week 8-10: Internal canary on non-customer pools, refine thresholds
Week 11-12: Pilot rollout to 3 customers, operational runbook and on-call playbook
Week 13: Post-pilot analysis and go/no-go for broad launch
deliverables: Design doc with algorithm math and failure modes
Console feature page with smoothing and hedging toggles
Pilot runbook and dashboards for unit cost, latency, queue length
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hedge algorithm underestimates spike leading to SLO miss -> Mitigation: conservative defaults and immediate failover to burst pools
Risk: Customers confused by smoothing changes to billing -> Mitigation: clear billing preview in Console and opt-in trial
Risk: Interaction with existing batching and cache policies causes unexpected token throughput -> Mitigation: test matrix across representative workloads before pilot
Risk: Overfitting pilot workloads -> Mitigation: choose pilots from distinct industries (SaaS chat, search, analytics)
dependencies_detail: ENG-8421: telemetry hooks for per-pool queue length and headroom metrics must be available
PM-23111: capacity hedging baseline research (uses earlier forecasting work)
stakeholders: Maya Chen (Console PM) - UI controls and billing preview
Ravi Gupta (SRE) - runbooks and on-call playbook
acceptance_criteria: Hedge algorithm implemented behind a feature flag and verified in simulation against historical traffic traces
Adaptive autoscale triggers implemented and covered by unit/integration tests
Console exposes three controls: smoothing window (hours), hedge percentage, and aggressive_failback toggle
Dashboards emit cost delta, queue length, and latency metrics for pilot pools
Pilot agreement signed by customers and pilot runbook executed without Severity 1 incidents
rollout_and_monitoring: Rollout steps: feature-flag internal -> limited internal customer pools -> 3 external pilots -> broad opt-in launch
Monitoring: per-pool P95/P99 latency, token throughput, queue length, autoscale event rate, monthly cost delta
Alerting: immediate pager for any P99 exceeding SLA for >2 consecutive autoscale windows
Fallback: automatic disable of smoothing for affected pools and revert to legacy autoscale policy
